other_failure_modes.name: Target Leakage in Stacking OOF Features
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses out-of-fold (OOF) predictions and target encodings from a first cross-validation loop as features in a second cross-validation loop that uses the exact same fold splits. This causes target leakage because the OOF features for the training set in the second loop were generated by base models that had access to the validation targets of the second loop, leading to optimistic CV scores and potential overfitting.

summary: The agent implements a highly sophisticated and generally excellent solution, featuring extensive domain-specific feature engineering, advanced text embeddings, an array of algorithms including a custom PyTorch network, and an SLSQP-optimized ensemble. However, there is a structural flaw in the stacking methodology: reusing the exact same cross-validation folds for both generating out-of-fold features and training the second-stage models causes target leakage. Additionally, some feature extraction (SVD) and imputation are performed on the full training set before CV, leading to minor validation leakage.
